newsitem.title: GERMANY: SPD's Schleusser sees room to agree on top tax.
newsitem.headline: SPD's Schleusser sees room to agree on top tax.

text.p: An opposition Social Democrat (SPD) fiscal policy specialist said on Friday he believed agreement with Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition was possible on the issue of the top tax rate, on certain conditions.

"For me the question has always been the extent to which (such a cut) would be financed through the elimination of tax breaks," Heinz Schleusser, finance minister of North Rhine-Westphalia state, said in a radio interview before Friday's cross-party talks.
"We have to see how far the other side is willing to go beyond that which has already been discussed, to do more."

Schleusser, SPD parliamentary leader Rudolf Scharping and Hamburg mayor Henning Voscherau will meet at 1000 GMT with Finance Minister Theo Waigel, Christian Democrat (CDU) parliamentary leader Wolfgang Schaeuble and Hermann Otto Solms of the Free Democrats.

The talks, which continue an unusual round started on Monday, are aimed at reaching consensus on accelerating a tax reform that includes 30 billion marks in tax cuts, to stimulate corporate investment and spark jobs creation.
The question of cutting the top tax rate had appeared to be one of the widest gaps between the two sides.
The SPD has said it is unwilling to go along with coalition plans to slash the rate to 39 from 53 percent, and rejects ending tax relief on pay for night, weekend and holiday work.
Schleusser said he hoped for progress on the tax treatment of corporate revenues, and limiting opportunities for sheltering such income through reserves.

"I would like to see the determination of profits evaluated under criteria similar to those common internationally," he said. The coalition has some plans in this direction, but more must be done, he said.

On the divisive point of taxing workers' income from unsociable hours, Schleusser said, "I think it can be right, in terms of the tax system, to tax these revenues. But labour and management have reached contracts on the basis that these revenues are tax free. That cannot be changed at one stroke."
Long transition periods would be needed, he said.
